summary: CardinalPay: fallback amplification causing repeated streaming truncation and billing spike - post-incident review
description: Issue summary: Between 2026-02-14 09:12 and 2026-02-14 11:03 UTC CardinalPay experienced repeated streaming truncations and an unexpected billing spike. The root trigger was a rollout of a quantized model variant plus an autoscale event on Dedicated capacity that caused the smart-routing fallback loop to amplify requests to higher-cost model variants and retried streaming sessions, producing duplicate billable tokens and truncated streams. Impact: customer-facing degradation (failed or truncated streaming responses), elevated 5xx for long-tail requests, and a ~3.7x increase in billed tokens for the customer during the window.
impact: All CardinalPay production tenants in us-east saw ~12% of streaming sessions truncated mid-response and a sudden 370% token billing spike for the 2-hour window. Latency SLOs breached for 98th/99th percentiles. Customer reported partial failures in live checkout flows and escalated to C-suite. Revenue-impacting and high-severity escalation.
environment_details: Dedicated GPU pool: dc-cardinal-us-east (A100, reserved), control plane: us-east-ctrl-01, route policy: cost-pref then latency fallback, model rollout: redwood-4b-quantized-8bit enabled for canary traffic at 09:05 UTC, autoscale event triggered at 09:11 UTC due to normal load blending.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer routing policy with cost-pref fallback enabled. 2) Roll out quantized variant redwood-4b-quantized-8bit to 10% canary. 3) Simulate load spike to trigger Dedicated autoscale (scale-up and immediate scheduling churn). 4) Observe smart-routing decisions and streaming sessions when primary nodes fail to accept new connections. Expected: graceful fallback once per request. Observed: rapid request fanout and repeated fallback/retry causing duplicate session starts and truncated streams.

investigation_notes: Timeline: - 09:05: canary of quantized variant enabled. - 09:11: Dedicated pool autoscaled (new nodes registered slowly; scheduling jitter observed). - 09:11-09:20: multiple routing decisions returned 'capacity_unavailable' transiently which triggered smart-routing to cascade fallbacks. - 09:12-09:45: API gateway retried streaming session startups on client reconnect which produced repeated partial streams. Hypothesis: the combination of slow node warm-up (KV cache coldness), scheduler churn, and an aggressive gateway retry policy led to duplicate requests being routed to fallback variants. Gateway retry and streaming reconnection logic did not de-duplicate session restarts. Confirmed by correlating session IDs and connection-attempt counters in gateway traces. Billing spike path: duplicate token accounting occurred because early-session partial outputs were counted as billable tokens before retries produced final responses; some retries were billed again by downstream accounting before final reconciliation.

resolution_summary: Root cause: interaction between quantized model canary rollout, Dedicated pool autoscale churn, and aggressive gateway retry behavior that led to repeated fallback routing and duplicate billable sessions. Fixes applied: 1) API gateway dedupe logic for streaming session restarts (patch deployed). 2) Scheduler tuning: increased node warm-up parallelism and image pull retry limits to reduce registration delay (PR merged). 3) Smart-routing change: temporary cooldown on consecutive fallbacks per-tenant to avoid amplification. Billing action: provisional credit approved and will be applied to CardinalPay March invoice.
follow_up_actions: 1) Postmortem doc created and linked: confluence.redwood.com/display/OPS/CardinalPay+INC+2026-02-14+Postmortem (owner: Marco Ruiz, due 2026-02-20). 2) Add automated test in CI that simulates canary rollout + autoscale to assert no routing amplification (owner: runtime team). 3) Billing: reconcile double-counted tokens and apply credit (owner: Sofia Park, ticket BILL-9876). 4) Product: review default gateway retry policy for streaming APIs and consider safer defaults (owner: Product infra). 5) Runbook update: add explicit guidance for coordinated model canary + autoscale during peak windows.
